summary: Kisin, Madapusi Pera and Shin show that the Newton strata of a Shimura variety of Hodge type are non-empty when the group G is quasi-split at p, confirming a conjecture of Fargues and Rapoport in that case, without assuming a good integral model (G may be ramified at p). They conjecture that every mod p isogeny class contains the reduction of a special point, a refinement of Honda–Tate theory, and prove a large part of this for PEL type, through Tate's theorem with additional structures, independence of ℓ and CM lifts. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and twelve findings are recorded, including a Weyl-group correction to Corollary 1.1.15 (E2), a counterexample to Lemma 2.2.11 as stated (E6) and the need for an ordinary class in §1.3.15 (E8). Not formalised.

items.statement: For a maximal Q_p-torus T' in G, ([b],{mu}) is T'-special if representatives b' in T'(L) and mu' in X_*(T') give a T'-admissible pair mapping to ([b],{mu}); special means this for some T'.

items.name: Elliptic torus supplies a basic admissible pair
items.statement: If [b] is basic and the pair is G-admissible, any elliptic maximal Q_p-torus T' and any representative mu' of {mu} in it supply the unique basic torus class mapping to [b].
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Unramified replacement preserving Galois averages
items.statement: For H=Res_(F/Qp) H0 with H0 absolutely simple quasi-split adjoint, there is an unramified F'/Q_p of equal degree and quasi-split unramified H0'/F' with an isomorphism of geometric based root data intertwining the averaging maps. This need not preserve the whole Galois action.

items.name: D4 triality orbit replacement
items.statement: In the noncyclic diagram-action case D4, the order-three subgroup of S3 has the same vertex orbits as S3; using it gives the same averaging on simple coroots, which suffices for N24.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Levi basic Newton formula
items.statement: For quasi-split G with standard Levi M and mu,mu_M having equal image in pi_1(G), the Newton point of the basic M-class with kappa_M=mu_M-sharp is the invariant rational central image of mu_M-sharp. Its G-admissibility is then exactly the Newton inequality.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Quasi-split minuscule Levi lift
items.statement: For quasi-split G/Q_p, standard Levi M, minuscule mu and basic [b_M] whose image is G-admissible, some w in W(G,T) makes ([b_M],{w mu}) M-admissible.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Torsion-free kernel in Levi coinvariants
items.statement: For the quasi-split standard Levi situation in Proposition 1.1.13, ker(pi_1(M)_Gamma to pi_1(G)_Gamma) is torsion free; intersecting it with the torsion kernel contributed by the central quotient kills the discrepancy.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: General rational-Levi minuscule lift (corrected: absolute Weyl group)
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over Q_p, M a Q_p-rational Levi subgroup, T⊂M a maximal torus, μ a minuscule cocharacter of M, and [b_M]∈B(M)_b such that ([b_M],{μ}) is G-admissible. Then there is w in the absolute Weyl group W(G,T)(Q̄_p), equivalently a G(Q̄_p)-conjugate μ′ of μ factoring through T, such that ([b_M],{w·μ}) is M-admissible. The printed requirement w∈N_G(M)/M is false, by the GL₃ example with M=GL₁×GL₂, μ=(0,1,0), b_M=diag(p,1,1) (errata E2).
items.note: Corrected formulation and proof supplied by the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5, 22 September 2026), following the structure of the paper's proof with the correct Weyl group. The only use, Corollary 1.1.17 (N32), needs exactly this: its proof writes "By Lemma 1.1.13, there exists w∈W(G,T)". The remaining inputs are N27 and its cited unramified result, and Kottwitz97 4.4, under G-local. The G-source gate for the normalizer statement is resolved by this correction.

items.name: Transfer of a maximal torus of J_b
items.statement: Under (1.1.3.1), a transfer of T' in J_b to M_[b] is a Q_p-embedding geometrically M_[b]-conjugate to its embedding under the inner twisting.

items.name: Existence of local torus transfer in the stated cases
items.statement: A maximal T' in J_b transfers to M_[b] if G is quasi-split or T' is elliptic. Rational transfer is stronger than geometric conjugacy.

items.name: Specialness for a transferred maximal torus
items.statement: Assume (1.1.3.1), minuscule admissible ([b],{mu}) and an existing transfer j:T' to M_[b]. Then the pair is j(T')-special and some mu_T' in the prescribed conjugacy class averages to nu_b,J. The non-quasi-split branch uses the corrected N29, with w in the absolute Weyl group W(G,T).

items.name: Prescribed real torus torsor trivial at p
items.statement: For any Q-torus T and prime p, ker(H1(Q,T) to H1(Q_p,T)) maps surjectively to H1(R,T).
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Local-global torus cohomology obstruction sequence
items.statement: For a Q-torus T, use the local cohomology-to-torsion-coinvariant maps and the exact sequence H1(Q,T) to direct-sum_v H1(Q_v,T) to X_*(T)_Gamma,tors. Its real-place map and normalization require the cited Kottwitz86 proof.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Auxiliary prime matching complex-conjugation action
items.statement: In a finite Galois splitting field of T choose an unramified ell distinct from p with Frobenius conjugate to complex conjugation; identify the associated local coinvariant torsion groups compatibly with the global obstruction. This gives the compensating class used in G01.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Approximation of maximal tori at finitely many places
items.statement: Given a connected reductive G/Q and maximal tori T_v over each of finitely many Q_v including possibly R, find a Q-torus T in G locally G(Q_v)-conjugate to T_v. This is approximation of torus embeddings, not weak approximation of every torus.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Simply connected local cohomology vanishing
items.statement: For a simply connected semisimple group H over a nonarchimedean completion Q_v, H1(Q_v,H) is trivial.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Steinberg torsor triviality over L
items.statement: For L=Frac W(Fpbar), connected reductive G-torsors are trivial. Prove the field/cohomological-dimension hypotheses and the finite-extension descent needed when an isomorphism is later realized over Q_(p^r).
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Real Weyl action and torus cocycle
items.statement: With T_sc anisotropic over R and a geometric Weyl element represented by n, n conjugate(n)^(-1) is a torus cocycle; its real H1 class depends only on the Weyl element.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Special Shimura pair with prescribed Newton class
items.statement: For a Shimura datum and admissible ([b],{mu_X inverse}) satisfying (1.1.3.1), construct a rational maximal torus T and x in X factoring through T whose basic torus class attached to mu_x inverse maps to [b]. The inverse is required; the displayed conclusion in §1.2.5 omits it.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Serre condition for a rational torus
items.statement: T/Q satisfies the Serre condition if its maximal R-split subtorus is defined and split over Q. Compact real quotient modulo rational scalars is a principal application.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Prime-unit in an algebraic group
items.statement: A rational point gamma of a Q-group is an l-unit if the cyclic subgroup it generates is bounded in H(Q_v) for every finite v distinct from l. For a torus this is equivalently unit valuations under all characters away from l.

items.name: Weil number and Weil point
items.statement: An l-Weil number is algebraic, an l-unit, and has all complex absolute values l^(w/2) for some integer w. A point is l-Weil when the eigenvalues in a faithful representation are l-Weil numbers; weights may vary until a separate uniform-weight theorem applies.

items.name: Representation independence of Weil points
items.statement: If the eigenvalues of gamma in one faithful representation are l-Weil, the same holds in every representation, by tensor generation, duality and subquotients; the weights need not be common in this general statement.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Serre condition converts units to Weil points
items.statement: For a Q-torus satisfying the Serre condition, gamma is l-Weil iff it is an l-unit. Prove the compact-subtorus quotient and character times conjugate-character calculation.

items.name: Neat semisimple point
items.statement: A point is neat here when it is semisimple and the Zariski closure of its cyclic group is connected, hence a torus. Distinguish this individual-point predicate from a neat level subgroup.

items.name: Zariski density of neat Weil points
items.statement: If T/Q satisfies the Serre condition and splits at l, its l-Weil points form a Zariski-dense subgroup; a fixed power of that subgroup consists of neat points and is still dense. Use a splitting field's finite roots of unity to kill the component groups.

items.name: Corrected finite-automorphism comparison on dense points
items.statement: For a reduced irreducible separated finite-type k-scheme S, a dense subset Gamma of S(k), finite W in Aut_k(S), and sigma in Aut_k(S) with sigma(gamma) in W.gamma for every gamma, some w in W equals sigma. Reducedness and a closed-equalizer hypothesis are explicit additions to the printed statement; the actual application is an affine torus.

items.name: Global transfer of maximal tori between inner forms
items.statement: A geometrically stable torus embedding into a quasi-split inner form which transfers locally at every place transfers globally in the setting of §2.2.14; retain its exact Langlands-Rapoport Lemma 5.6 hypotheses.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Simply connected derived group and abelianized obstruction
items.statement: For connected reductive G/Q with simply connected derived group, a G-torsor trivial in H1(R,G) and in H1(Q,G_ab) is trivial, under Borovoi Theorem 5.12 as used in §2.3.14.

items.name: Hasse obstruction for the abelian quotient
items.statement: ker1(Q,G_ab) is the kernel of H1(Q,G_ab) to the product over all places of H1(Q_v,G_ab). Its vanishing is a separate hypothesis, not automatic for all tori.

items.statement: At the lattice-stabilizer level of §1.3.2 and a place v of E above p, take the normalization of the closure of the generic Hodge-type Shimura variety in the ambient Siegel model over O_(E,v). items.statement: For each absolute Hodge tensor, its pointwise crystalline realizations S03 come from a morphism 1 to D-tensor in F-Isoc of the entire special fiber, including its nonsmooth loci.

items.statement: The realization V to D extends to an exact faithful tensor functor Rep_Qp(G) to F-Isoc of the geometric special fiber. Prove tensor generation and descent; do not identify the monodromy subgroup with all of G solely because selected tensors are preserved.

items.name: Closed lower Newton locus
items.statement: For every geometric point x, the set of x' with bar-nu([b_x']) dominated by bar-nu([b_x]) is Zariski closed in the geometric special fiber.

items.name: Nonempty locally closed Newton strata
items.statement: For [b] in B(G,{mu_X inverse}) satisfying (1.1.3.1), the locus S_[b]={x:[b_x]=[b]} is nonempty and locally closed. Local closedness is obtained from the finite dominance interval and constant Kottwitz condition.

items.name: Newton closure inclusion
items.statement: The Zariski closure of S_[b] is contained in the union of S_[b'] with bar-nu([b']) dominated by bar-nu([b]). Equality is not asserted at general level.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Mu-ordinary locus from an actual ordinary class
items.statement: Given an inhabitant of C10 for the inverse Hodge cocharacter class {μ_X^{-1}}, define its Newton stratum as the μ-ordinary locus. The class is unique, but can fail to exist for inner forms (C07–C08). A greatest admissible class alone does not define this locus.

items.name: Openness and nonemptiness of the mu-ordinary stratum
items.statement: Given S15, a rational Newton representative (1.1.3.1), the Newton finiteness/semicontinuity interface and S07, its stratum is nonempty and open. Quasi-split G supplies the two algebraic hypotheses by C02 and N16. The class-existence assertion is false for arbitrary inner forms.

items.name: Density under local integrality
items.statement: In the setting of S15–S16, if the special fiber is locally integral, the mu-ordinary stratum is dense. Prove irreducibility of special fibers of connected components and transport nonemptiness between components by level-changing isogenies.
items.note: The algebraic ordinary-existence scope is now resolved by C02/C07. The compactification/component argument and level-changing Hecke transport still require the original MP19 proof. Local integrality alone is not replaced by the local quaternion calculation.

items.name: Hyperspecial density specialization
items.statement: For p>2 and hyperspecial K_p arising from the reductive integral model, the source's smooth integral model satisfies the local-integrality hypothesis and hence the mu-ordinary locus is dense.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Tame special-parahoric density specialization
items.statement: Conditional safe contract: for p>2, tamely split G, the prescribed special-parahoric normal model and an actual ordinary class satisfying (1.1.3.1), a Hodge embedding with locally integral special fiber permits S17. Before asserting the printed unconditional scope, audit KP18 Corollary 0.3, its quasi-split and vertex hypotheses, and comparison of special versus very special parahorics.
items.note: The local counterexample C07 rules out dropping ordinary existence for arbitrary inner forms. It does not by itself settle which hypotheses the geometric KP18 application supplies.

items.name: Prime-to-p integral tower
items.statement: Form the inverse limit over sufficiently small away-p levels with finite-etale transition maps; its points carry an abelian object, polarization and full prime-to-p level trivialization. Extend the right G(A_f^p) action by normality with the fixed p-level.

items.statement: Construct Aut_Q(A) as the unit group scheme of End(A) tensor Q, with its action on all etale Tate and crystalline realizations. Rationalizing a Hom group is not a change of the ground field of A.

items.name: Stable ell-adic Frobenius centralizer
items.statement: For ell distinct from p, I_ell,x is the eventual centralizer in G_Qell of gamma_m,ell,x for sufficiently divisible m. Stabilization is under divisibility, not arbitrary large integers; the group is connected reductive once the cyclic Frobenius closure is a torus.

api.name: KMPS.T08.centralizer

api.name: KMPS.T08.injection

items.name: Split auxiliary-prime comparison
items.statement: If ell differs from p, G_Qell is split and the characteristic polynomial of a sufficiently divisible Frobenius splits over Q_ell, the injection I_x tensor Q_ell to I_ell,x is an isomorphism.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Finiteness-to-group comparison argument
items.statement: The fixed-level finite set S_K(F_(q^m)) bounds I_x(Q_ell)\I_ell,x(Q_ell)/(K_ell intersect I_ell,x); prove the precise reductive-group lemma showing this finite quotient forces the split auxiliary-prime injection to be onto.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Finite-field crystalline descent and Frobenius norm
items.statement: Over Q_(q^m)=W(F_(q^m))[1/p], after sufficiently divisible m choose a tensor trivialization with F=delta sigma. Then gamma_m,p=delta sigma(delta)...sigma^(rm-1)(delta) for q=p^r.

api.name: KMPS.T11.descentField

items.name: Crystalline stable centralizer
items.statement: I_(m,delta)(R)={g in G(Q_(q^m) tensor R):g delta=delta sigma(g)}; after scalar extension it is the centralizer of gamma_m,p. Its stabilized value I_p,x embeds in J_delta; equality with all of J_delta is not assumed.

api.name: KMPS.T12.toSigmaCentralizer
api.statement: Embed into J_delta while retaining the finite-field descent condition.

items.name: Semisimple conjugacy quotient
items.statement: For connected reductive H over a characteristic-zero field, Conj(H)=Spec(O(H)^H) parametrizes semisimple geometric conjugacy classes. Rational quotient points are not asserted to be rational conjugacy classes of H(F).

items.name: Type-D adjusted conjugacy quotient
items.statement: Form Out'(H) from the O(2n)/SO(2n) symmetries of the indicated derived SO factors with n>=4, descend its finite action, and define Conj'(H)=Conj(H)/Out'(H). Include central-isogeny and factor-identification compatibility before using this as a functor.

api.name: KMPS.T14.noTypeD

items.name: Noot independence of Frobenius conjugacy class
items.statement: For the reductions and sufficiently divisible Frobenius in this Hodge-type setup, the classes gamma_m,ell in Conj'(G) are one rational class independent of ell, including the crystalline realization at p. This is the specific input quoted from Noot, not a general compatible-system axiom.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Tate theorem for automorphisms with tensors at every prime
items.statement: For every ell, including p, I_x tensor Q_ell to I_ell,x is an isomorphism. Use the auxiliary-prime isomorphism and equal centralizer dimensions from Conj'(G), together with connectedness of the target. Consequently I_x is connected and has rank G.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Common weight of a Weil quasi-endomorphism
items.statement: If gamma in I_x(Q) is l-Weil, the eigenvalue multiset on V_Qell is independent of ell distinct from p, and all eigenvalues have a single l-Weil weight. Use the polarization character and the compact real isometry subgroup; this is stronger than G12.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Admissible classical representation for Noot's argument
items.statement: For an absolutely almost simple classical group, an admissible representation is a positive multiple of the specified A standard-plus-dual, B spin, C standard, D standard or D two-half-spin representation; distinguish D^H and D^R. This use of admissible is unrelated to B(G,mu).

items.name: Accommodating symplectic embedding
items.statement: A strictly accommodating Hodge embedding has the restriction-of-scalars, admissible-representation, D^R character-part and minimality properties listed in §2.2.6. An accommodating embedding is assembled from strictly accommodating factors with derived groups matching; the printed recursive wording must be checked against Noot's definition.

items.name: Conjugacy independence for neat Weil points
items.statement: For any neat Weil point gamma of I_x(Q), the image of i_ell(gamma) in Conj'(G) is a rational point independent of ell, including p.

items.name: Accommodating-case character-polynomial argument
items.statement: For an accommodating embedding, decompose the faithful representation into its algebraic isotypic factors and use independent factor characteristic polynomials, neatness and Noot's reconstruction lemmas to recover a common Conj' class.

items.name: Auxiliary accommodating Shimura correspondence
items.statement: Construct (G'',X'') from a common adjoint datum of (G,X) and an accommodating (G',X'), with V''=V direct-sum V'; lift the point, prove good reduction, and compare tensor-preserving groups using the projectors. The identifications modulo centers require T16.

items.name: Rational abelian-quotient map
items.statement: There is a Q-group map I_x→G_ab whose base change equals the maps induced by i_ℓ for every ℓ. The auxiliary Shimura datum must be G′=G×_{G^ab}T, pairs (g,t) with the same image in G^ab, not the printed G×T.
items.note: Repair and proof supplied by the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5, 22 September 2026). With the printed G′=G×T the construction fails twice: G×T is not in GSp(V⊕V,ψ⊕ψ), and the kernel of I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀} contains 1×T, which maps onto G^ab. This is recorded in research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22.json (E5). The remaining inputs, Corollary 2.1.9 and Noot, stay under G-noot.

items.name: Conjugacy of realization embeddings
items.statement: The embeddings i_ell:I_x to G, defined over Q_ell for ell distinct from p and sufficiently large unramified Q_p-extensions at p, are conjugate over a common algebraically closed overfield by Aut'(G). If G_ad has no type-D factor they are conjugate by G.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Rational transfer of a maximal isogeny torus
items.statement: If G is quasi-split at p and G_ad has no type-D factor, every maximal T in I_x has a Q-embedding in G geometrically conjugate to each i_ell restricted to T; every Frobenius gamma_m then has a representative gamma_m,0 in G(Q) in its common geometric class.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Rational isogeny Isom scheme
items.statement: For geometric abelian varieties A,A', represent R-isogenies in R tensor_Q Hom_Q(A,A') as the invertible locus; it is empty or a torsor under Aut_Q(A). R is a coefficient algebra, not the characteristic-p base field.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Classical Tate isogeny comparison
items.statement: For abelian varieties over a finite field after sufficiently divisible finite extension, rational Hom tensor Q_ell equals Frobenius-equivariant Hom on Tate modules for ell distinct from p, and the contravariant crystalline counterpart for ell=p. Restrict to invertible maps to compare T26 with realization Isom schemes.
items.note: Finite-field Tate comparison co-owned with the current PAPER-SMITH-24 source route at R28.4. Keep its proof separate from the number-field Faltings argument; the crystalline p-part is an explicit added supplier obligation.

items.name: Tensor-preserving isogeny torsors
items.statement: P_ell(x,x') is the closed realization Isom subscheme preserving every specified Hodge tensor; P(x,x') is the largest Q-closed subscheme mapping into all P_ell, including p. Each is empty or a torsor under its corresponding automorphism group.

items.name: Tate-with-tensors comparison hypothesis
items.statement: Define the additional hypothesis TT(x,x') to mean P(x,x') tensor Q_ell to P_ell(x,x') is an isomorphism for every ell. The assertion for all pairs is Conjecture 2.3.4, not a proved general theorem. The diagonal case follows from T16.

items.name: Independence from a generating tensor family
items.statement: The torsors P and P_ell and the comparison hypothesis depend on the two Shimura points rather than the chosen tensor family defining G; compare both to their union and identify nonemptiness through the common Frobenius conjugacy class.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Tate-with-tensors for PEL A and C
items.statement: For PEL type A or C, endomorphisms and polarization similitudes define G, and classical Tate comparison restricts to the tensor-preserving torsors. Thus TT(x,x') holds for all pairs.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Geometric versus rational coefficient isogeny
items.statement: Call x,x' Qbar-isogenous when P(x,x') is nonempty geometrically, and Q-isogenous when P(x,x')(Q) is nonempty. Geometric nonemptiness is not a rational section and does not make the torsor trivial.

items.name: CM lift with respect to a maximal torus
items.statement: For maximal T in I_x, a CM lift consists of a rational embedding j:T to G conjugate to all local embeddings, a point z in X factoring through j(T_R), and x' reducing a point of the associated torus Shimura variety; require a geometric or rational coefficient isogeny to x as specified.

items.name: Special-torus Frobenius is a prime-unit
items.statement: For a special-point reduction x associated with (T,z), its sufficiently divisible q^m-Frobenius gamma_m,x belongs to T(Q) and is a p-unit.

items.name: Uniqueness of special torus Frobenius up to finite order
items.statement: Two T(Q)-points satisfying the same p-unit and Kottwitz valuation conditions have a ratio of finite order. Use discreteness in finite adeles for this compact-mod-scalars torus and compactness of the local valuation kernel; do not assert finite-adelic discreteness for arbitrary Q-tori.

items.name: Conditional geometric CM lift
items.statement: If G is quasi-split at p, G_ad has no type-D factor and TT holds for all point pairs, every x and maximal T in I_x admit a Qbar-isogeny CM lift with respect to T. The construction must use the inverse Hodge cocharacter consistently.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: Torus reduction of the isogeny torsor
items.statement: Given a geometric CM lift with respect to T, the subfunctor P^T of tensor-preserving isogenies commuting with T is a T-torsor. Its image in H1(Q_v,G) is trivial for every place v, including R and p.

items.name: Rational CM lift from a Hasse principle
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of T36, if G_der is simply connected and ker1(Q,G_ab)=0, every x and maximal T admit a Q-isogeny CM lift. Trivializing the pushed-forward G-torsor changes the torus embedding and CM point; it does not assert the original P^T is already trivial.

items.name: PEL geometric CM lifts
items.statement: If G is quasi-split at p and the datum is PEL of type A or C, every point and every maximal torus of I_x admit a Qbar-isogeny CM lift with respect to that torus.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.

items.name: PEL rational CM lifts in the stated cases
items.statement: Under the PEL and quasi-split-at-p hypotheses of T39, type C and type A_n with n odd admit Q-isogeny CM lifts for each maximal T, preserving endomorphisms and polarization up to rational scalar. The unitary n-even, odd-[F+:Q] extension is a separate assertion T43.

items.name: Type-D disconnected-group variant
items.statement: For PEL type D replace G by the full possibly disconnected stabilizer G' of endomorphisms and polarization; the source sketches a geometric-isogeny CM lift statement defined by those tensors. It does not establish the identical connected-G torsor statement; the exercise's proof is an open extraction leaf.

items.name: Unpolarized isogeny torsors split
items.statement: If the isogeny condition retains only the endomorphism data, the automorphism group is the unit group of a product of semisimple algebras and the nonempty Isom torsor has a rational point by the open subset argument in a rational vector space. This recovers the stated comparison with Zink but does not remove the polarization obstruction in T38.

items.statement: A p-adic formal log scheme over W carries compatible fine saturated log structures on its reductions modulo p^n, with exact transition closed immersions.

items.statement: An enlargement of X/W is a p-adic formal log scheme T, an ideal of definition I, and a log map T_0=V(I) to X. It is reduced when T_0 is reduced, and a PD enlargement includes divided powers on I extending those on pW.

items.statement: For flat normal finite-type S/W, relative Cartier divisor D and U=S minus D, an abelian scheme over U extending semi-abelianly over S supplies a log Dieudonne crystal and E_log restricting to E on U, compatibly with Cartier duality. Use the divisorial log structure O_S intersect j_*O_U^units; the printed U=D minus S is reversed.

items.statement: For proper semistable S/O_K with S_0 union D normal crossings, enlarge the boundary log structure D by S_0 to obtain S_vlog and E_vlog=i* E_log. Keep the two log structures distinct on the same underlying scheme.

items.statement: Association yields a Frobenius-invariant horizontal section on the first enlargement; suitable Frobenius rescaling and Tate twists permit mixed tensor-duals, and Frobenius invariance extends it through all R_n. Prove compatibility, not just existence on each chart.

items.statement: If S is proper semistable over O_K and S_0 union D is normal crossings, there is s_0:1 to E_log-tensor whose evaluation at every permitted integral point equals s_(0,xi). Glue the horizontal enlargement sections and prove functoriality.

items.name: Compact real polarization-isometry group
items.statement: For a polarized abelian variety, the real points of the group {g in (End(A) tensor R)^units: g^dagger g=1} are compact. Scalar similitudes yield a compact quotient modulo real scalar multiplication.

items.name: Hasse principle for simply connected semisimple groups
items.statement: For a simply connected semisimple group H over Q, ker(H1(Q,H) to product_v H1(Q_v,H)) is trivial. The real-place condition remains part of the hypothesis.

items.name: PEL abelian quotient Hasse cases
items.statement: For the PEL type-C groups, and the source type-A_n groups with n odd, ker1(Q,G_ab)=0, as invoked from Kottwitz92 §7. This does not assert the conclusion for all type-A_n groups.

items.name: Odd-degree unitary Hasse case
items.statement: For the unitary similitude group in n+1 variables attached to a CM quadratic extension F/F+ with n even and [F+:Q] odd, the Hasse principle for G follows by Shin11 Lemma 3.1.1 as invoked in Remark 2.3.16(1). items.name: Torus Newton invariant is the Galois average
items.statement: For an F=Q_p torus T and λ∈X_*(T), let [b_T]=κ_T^{-1}([λ]). Then ν_T(b_T)=N_Γ λ in X_*(T)_Q^Γ. The average is rational; κ_T still retains integral coinvariant torsion.

items.name: Ordinary class for a quasi-split group
items.statement: For connected reductive G/Q_p quasi-split, any geometric cocharacter class {μ} has a unique [b_μ]∈B(G,{μ}) with ν=μ^diamond. Choose a Q_p-rational Borel pair T⊂B and B-dominant μ∈X_*(T). The image of κ_T^{-1}([μ]) has the required invariants. A rational Newton representative exists. This algebraic existence statement does not by itself prove density in an integral model.

items.name: Quaternion division algebra and its split Frobenius model
items.statement: Fix F=Q_p, its unramified quadratic extension E with automorphism τ, and D=E⊕E j with j²=p and j a=τ(a)j. Then D is a division algebra. Over L=breve Q_p, identify D_L with M_2(L) by a↦diag(a,τa) and j↦J=[[0,p],[1,0]]. The F-descent operator is σ_D(A)=J σ(A) J^{-1}; σ_D²=σ². Put G=D^×.

items.statement: With C03, b↦bJ gives a bijection B(D^×)→B(GL_2), where the left uses σ_D and the right uses σ. It is not a homomorphism or an invariant-preserving identification. κ_GL2(bJ)=κ_D(b)+1.

items.statement: For C03 and C04, if the ordinary GL_2-isocrystal (bJ)σ has dominant slopes (a,c), the dominant Newton vector for b with descent σ_D is (a−1/2,c−1/2).

items.name: Two distinct rank-two slopes are integral
items.statement: For a two-dimensional isocrystal over Frac W(Fpbar), two distinct slopes must both be integers. Each distinct slope space has dimension one. This consequence uses the rank-one classification and slope decomposition, not a claim that all-rank classification exists in Mathlib.

items.name: Quaternion obstruction to an ordinary class
items.statement: For G=D^× from C03 and any integer m, let {μ_m} have split dominant representative (m+1,m). Then B(G,{μ_m}) has no class with Newton vector μ_m^diamond=(m+1,m). In particular μ=(1,0) and the inverse-Hodge class represented dominantly by (0,−1) both fail ordinary existence.

items.name: A unique maximal admissible class need not be ordinary
items.statement: For C07, B(D^×,{μ_m}) is a singleton. Its representative is b=p^m J and its Newton vector is (m+1/2,m+1/2), strictly below μ_m^diamond. Thus its unique greatest class is basic and is not μ-ordinary.

items.name: Rational cocharacters of a division algebra are central
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional division algebra D/F, every F-morphism λ:G_m→D^× is λ(t)=t^n·1 for an integer n. Every rational F-defined cocharacter is central. In C03 the basic class C08 has a rational Newton representative, but the noncentral orbit (m+1,m) has none.

items.name: Ordinary Newton class with an explicit witness
items.statement: For connected reductive G/Q_p and a cocharacter class {μ}, OrdinaryClass(G,{μ}) consists of an actual [b]∈B(G), the equality κ_G(b)=μ^sharp and the equality ν_G(b)=μ^diamond. It is a subsingleton by N11 and can be empty. A rational Newton representative is separate data required by the geometric nonemptiness theorem.

items.statement: If G is quasi-split at p, then for every s_0 ∈ S_Kp(F̄_p) and every maximal torus T ⊂ I_s0, s_0 admits an isogeny CM lift with respect to T.
